genre: post-orbital ocean monastery, salvage ethics, signal economy
premise: A monastery built around a crashed communications satellite sits below a stormy sea dome where bandwidth is a holy relic.
simulation_objective: Simulate a high-stakes economy of signal salvage and pressure-suit maintenance.
economy_focus: Bandwidth vouchers and pressure-resistant salvage components.
exploration_focus: Submerged satellite arrays and pressurized trade corridors.
conflict_tone: Commercial rivalry and theological disputes over signal purity.
visual_style: Deep sea industrial with glowing fiber-optic vestments.

social_rules: Bandwidth is sacred; siphoning is a crime punishable by air-rationing.
Pressure suits must be inspected weekly by a certified engineer.
All salvage from the satellite belongs to the Abbot, minus a 20% finder's fee.
Silence must be observed during the 'Great Ping' at midnight.
player_entry_points: Arriving as a new pilgrim on a supply sub.
Waking up in the med-bay after a salvage accident.
Being hired as a freelance security consultant.
conflict_hooks: The main satellite array is failing, and only illegal salvage can fix it.
A Signal Pirate has stolen the Abbot's master keycard.
The sea dome has developed a crack that the monks are hiding.

gameplay_loops.label: The Signal Economy
